transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?

Honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is that my shoulders and neck are clenched all day. It feels like I’m bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. By evening my jaw aches so much I can barely enjoy playing guitar.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different everyday things, such as work, family, or routine responsibilities?

Yes. My mind goes from one thing to another constantly—whether I’ll ever get hired again, whether I’ve ruined my reputation with parents, whether retirement is slipping away. And then I’ll fixate on some small mistake during story time and think maybe I shouldn’t be trusted with children at all.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worry?
About a year and two months now—since I was fired from the preschool.
Alongside this worry, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I know I’m worried all the time, but I don’t know if I’d call it feeling depressed most of the day.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop these worries once they start?

Yes, very. I try to redirect myself—make a list, pray, weed the garden, focus on the next practical step—but one worry just turns into another. Before I know it, I’ve lost half the afternoon going over everything in my head.
Have you been having trouble with your sleep, such as falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yes. Most nights I’m lying there for hours replaying interview answers, bills, licensing forms—everything. And when I do get to sleep, I usually wake up around four already tense, trying to figure out what could go wrong that day.
